data.reasoning: The package is a standard Electron wrapper that downloads a pinned tarball from GitHub, verifies it with a SHA256 checksum, and copies files into place during the package() function. There are no build or prepare steps that execute arbitrary code, no .install hooks, and no suspicious network operations. The disagreement was solely due to a transient API error (HTTP 400) in the first report when auditing .SRCINFO, which the second report successfully completed and found safe.
data.disagreement_analysis: The first report (qwen3) resulted in 'inconclusive' purely because of a tool error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) when auditing .SRCINFO. The second report (deepseek-v4-flash) successfully audited both files and found them safe. There was no substantive disagreement on the code itself.
coverage_issues: qwen3-235b-a22b-2507 failed to audit .SRCINFO due to an LLM API error (HTTP 400), resulting in an inconclusive package verdict.
learnings: Implement retry logic or graceful degradation for transient LLM API errors (e.g., HTTP 400/500) so a single file failure doesn't force an inconclusive package verdict when the remaining files are safe.
Models correctly skipped upstream source fetching for a package with no build/prepare steps, demonstrating good judgment in avoiding unnecessary work for simple file-copying packages.
